correctness.rationale: The strongly positive first-return code has unique marked boundaries, uniformly bounded in a finite core. The induced finite-alphabet suspension and Gibbs inequality derive the unique pressure equation. At h=log2 the Catalan coefficient masses sum to 1/2. With t=2N(log2−h), the exact renewal equation has coefficients a_n=C_(n−1)/4^n~(4sqrt(pi))^(−1)n^(−3/2). At t=0.5 log N+log log N+c, the lower-half exponential perturbation is o(1); endpoint Laplace for the upper half yields limit 1/2+exp(c)/(2sqrt(pi)). Strict monotonicity then squeezes the unique root to c=0.5 log pi. No unproved infinite extrapolation from the finite checker is involved. Boundary N=1 gives h=0; N>1 gives 0<h<log2.

value.rationale: The primitive positive-excursion presentation is a natural and explicitly studied example where the qualitative finite-core approximation converges to entropy log2 but has no rate in the source. The entropy-root threshold exhibits a nontrivial critical n^(−3/2) endpoint phenomenon: finite cores only close the gap at scale (log N)/N with the additional loglog N and pi constant. This exact quantitative answer is pertinent to finite-core approximations and cannot be inferred from the Catalan counts or root computations without the analysis. It is not framed as a general theorem for arbitrary enumerations.
